candidate: NOV005 - Hydroxamic acid-tropolone hybrid (Rank 1 by composite score)
rationale_for_selection: NOV005 combines the established Cu-chelating enol of tropolone (REF004, Vina -5.73) with a C2-hydroxamic acid arm. This dual-chelation motif targets BOTH Cu ions simultaneously: the enol O and ketone O of the tropolone ring coordinate CuA, while the hydroxamic acid -C(=O)NHOH coordinates CuB through its carbonyl and hydroxyl oxygens. Design precedent: hydroxamic acids are known metalloprotease inhibitors (HDAC, MMP); their Cu-chelation mode is well-established (Zhou et al. J Med Chem 2019).

steps.description: Synthesis of tropolone-2-carboxylic acid from tropolone
steps.reaction: Tropolone + CO2 (Kolbe-Schmitt) or via direct carboxylation
steps.actual_route: Simpler route: Tropolone -> 2-methoxycarbonyltropolone via methyl chloroformate (Et3N, DCM, 0?C). Tropolone is commercial (Sigma, ~$25/g, CAS 533-75-5)

steps.description: Hydroxamic acid formation from methyl ester
steps.reaction: Methyl tropolone-2-carboxylate + NH2OH?HCl + NaOMe -> hydroxamic acid
steps.conditions: NH2OH?HCl (1.5 eq), NaOMe (3 eq), MeOH, 0?C -> RT, 2h
steps.yield_expected: 50-70% based on analogous hydroxamic acid syntheses
steps.notes: Hydroxamic acid formation from esters with NH2OH is general and high-yielding. Literature: Jayaram et al. Bioorg Med Chem Lett 2017 for analogous tropolone-hydroxamic hybrids.

green_chemistry_note: Both steps use mild conditions; MeOH solvent recyclable; no heavy metal catalysis required
literature_precedent: Tropolone as tyrosinase inhibitor: Kahn & Andrawis (1985) Phytochemistry 24:905
Hydroxamic acid Cu-chelation: Zhou et al. (2019) J Med Chem 62:4874
Tropolone-hydroxamic acid hybrids: Jayaram et al. (2017) Bioorg Med Chem Lett 27:3016
